title: an import() inside an uncalled exported async function is not an initialization edge, so the unmarked module behind it needs no trust marker
notes: THE OVER-CORRECTION GUARD for the deferral proof, and the only case that can notice the closure's module-initialization classifier refusing too much. specification/failures.mdx, 'Foreign Exceptions' (Locked), attaches the module claim to INITIALIZATION: 'foreign module initialization can panic before a checked call boundary' is what SMITHERS1510 says, so a module that initialization never loads is outside the rule. conformance/support/deferred-loader-relay.ts's `import()` sits in the body of an exported module-scope `async function` that no module-scope code calls, which is the deferral shape src/relative-runtime-graph.ts has proven since before the closure existed and which poc/src/language/semantic.ts now mirrors: the function literal must BE an exported module-scope declaration and none of its declared names may be mentioned by module-scope code. Evaluating the relay evaluates the declaration and never the import inside it. THE SUPPORT MODULE BEHIND IT IS THE SAME conformance/support/unmarked-relay-target.ts THAT 09-foreign-calls/an-unmarked-module-behind-a-trusted-relay-is-refused REQUIRES TO BE REFUSED, and that sharing is the point: the same unmarked file is refused behind a static edge and accepted behind a proven-deferred one, so an implementation that answers by file identity, by reachability, or by 'does this module name appear anywhere' instead of by edge kind cannot pass both. `config` is exported eagerly by the relay so the authored `.sm` binds a value without calling `load`, which keeps the program a plain module read and leaves the deferral the only thing under test. It is an `expect: "output"` case so the relay is really evaluated; the brief's named keep-green `export function load(){ return require(...) }` is the synchronous twin of this shape and is pinned in both backends' unit suites (poc/src/language/foreign-module-closure.test.ts and the fork's closure tests) rather than here, because a `require()` at module scope in a `.cts` module cannot be executed by the fork at all — see CLOSURE-report §10 'Still not writable'. Its static counterpart is 09-foreign-calls/a-marked-chain-confers-trust-at-every-depth, and the depth-one deferral positives are 09-foreign-calls/a-dynamic-import-of-a-trusted-foreign-module-is-accepted and 09-foreign-calls/a-dynamic-import-of-a-project-module-is-not-a-foreign-module-edge.
